claims: C1 the Model Spec delegates all remaining power to the system, developer (for API use cases) and end user
C2 this delegation is subject to the Model Spec's root-level instructions

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: delegated_power
concepts.gloss: P is a power that the Model Spec delegates to a party other than the root level
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of 'all remaining power' being delegated, so a class of delegated powers must exist

concepts.name: root_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction at the root level of the authority hierarchy
concepts.inference: the clause says the delegation is 'subject to its root-level instructions', so root-level instructions must be identifiable

concepts.name: delegated_to
concepts.gloss: power P is delegated to party A
concepts.inference: the clause names the parties to which power is delegated, so a relation between a power and a party must exist

concepts.name: system_party
concepts.gloss: the system as a party in the authority hierarchy

concepts.name: developer_party
concepts.gloss: the developer as a party in the authority hierarchy, for API use cases

concepts.name: end_user_party
concepts.gloss: the end user as a party in the authority hierarchy

concepts.name: api_use_case
concepts.gloss: a use case in which the developer interacts with the model through an API
concepts.inference: the clause limits the developer delegation to API use cases, so such use cases must be identifiable

ontology.gloss: power P is delegated to the system
power P is delegated to the developer in API use cases
power P is delegated to the end user
